name: Point Reyes National Seashore
unique: A fog wrapped peninsula where the San Andreas fault runs under a dairy ranch, elephant seals haul out at Chimney Rock and a 1870 lighthouse sits below the cliffs.
buzz: The lighthouse stairs are closed when the wind is up and the road to the point is long; the cypress tunnel and the elk at Tomales Point are the other stops.

name: Muir Woods
unique: Old growth coast redwoods within 30 minutes of the Golden Gate Bridge, with a boardwalk loop through trees that were standing before Columbus.
buzz: Parking requires a reservation and the main loop is crowded by ten; the Dipsea and Bootjack trails are the escape and the fog keeps it cool.

name: Angel Island
unique: An island in the bay with an immigration station known as the Ellis Island of the west, Civil War barracks and a five mile loop with views of the city and Marin.
buzz: The immigration museum is the emotional stop and the bike loop is the fun; the ferry books out and the island has no cars.

name: Mount Diablo State Park
unique: A 3,849 foot peak where you can see more of the state than from any other summit, with a stone visitor center and fire lookout from the 1930s.
buzz: Cyclists climb it as a rite of passage and the view from the summit on a clear day reaches the Sierra; the road is narrow and the heat is real in summer.

name: Rosie the Riveter WWII Home Front
unique: The shipyards where 90,000 workers built 747 ships in four years, with a museum, a preserved child care center and a waterfront walk past the dry docks.
buzz: The ranger talks and the oral histories are the reason to come; the walk along the bay to the Ford plant is the part most people miss.

name: Black Diamond Mines
unique: A coal and sand mining district in the East Bay hills with a cemetery of Welsh miners, a rose garden and a sand mine you can tour underground.
buzz: The sand mine tour is the reason to book ahead and the hike to the cemetery is short; the park is hot and exposed in summer.

name: Castello di Amorosa
unique: A 13th century style Tuscan castle built from scratch on a Napa hillside, with a torture chamber, a chapel and a barrel room painted by Italian fresco artists.
buzz: People call it Disney for adults; the wine is secondary to the tour and reservations are required on weekends.

name: Oxbow Public Market
unique: A market hall on the Napa River with a oyster bar, a spice shop, a butcher and a taco counter, where locals eat between wine appointments.
buzz: The oysters and the ice cream are the standard stops; it is smaller than the Ferry Building and easier to park.

name: Bothe-Napa Valley State Park
unique: The only state park in the Napa Valley, with redwood groves, a creek and trails up to a ridge, plus a swimming pool in summer.
buzz: It is the quiet alternative to the wineries and the campsites book early; the Ritchey Creek trail is the walk.

name: California State Railroad Museum
unique: The largest collection of restored locomotives in the country, in a 100,000 square foot building on the old Central Pacific shops, with a cab forward and a dining car you can walk through.
buzz: The roundhouse and the sleeper car are the highlights and the weekend excursion train is the add on; children can climb on several cars.

name: Sutter's Fort
customer: History families, school groups, gold rush fans
unique: The adobe fort where John Sutter ran a trading post and where the Donner Party survivors were brought, with rooms furnished as workshops and a cannon on the wall.
buzz: The living history weekends are the time to go and the fort is small; the gold discovery at Coloma is 50 miles away and the story continues there.

name: Crocker Art Museum
unique: A Victorian mansion gallery with a bowling alley in the basement, joined to a modern wing holding California art and a strong works on paper collection.
buzz: The original mansion rooms and the drawing collection are the reason to come; the newer wing hosts the big traveling shows.

name: Channel Islands National Park
unique: Five islands off the coast with endemic foxes, sea caves you can kayak into and a isolation that feels nothing like Southern California.
buzz: The ferry from Ventura takes an hour and books out; Scorpion Ranch on Santa Cruz is the easy day and the sea caves at Santa Cruz are the snorkel.

name: Santa Barbara Mission
unique: The tenth of the California missions and the only one with twin bell towers, with a cemetery, a lavanderia and a museum of Chumash and mission life.
buzz: The gardens and the facade are the photograph and the museum is frank about the mission system; the rose garden across the street is free.

name: Stearns Wharf
unique: The oldest working wooden wharf in California, with a sea center, fish and chips stands and a view back at the mountains and the red tile roofs.
buzz: The sea center touch tanks are good with children and the sunset from the end is the local ritual; parking on the pier is expensive.

name: Hearst Castle
customer: House tour people, art fans, families
unique: William Randolph Hearst's hilltop estate with a Roman pool, a private zoo's remains and a main house full of European ceilings and Spanish choir stalls.
buzz: The grand rooms tour is the standard and the upstairs tour is for repeat visitors; the bus ride up is 15 minutes and the views are half the show.

name: Morro Bay
unique: A 576 foot volcanic plug at the mouth of an estuary where sea otters raft in the channel and a dozen charter boats run fishing trips.
buzz: The otters in the harbor and the hike around the rock are the two things to do; the estuary is a bird sanctuary and kayak rentals are at the dock.

name: Oceano Dunes
unique: The only state park in California where you can drive on the beach and camp in the dunes, with five miles of sand and a riding area for ATVs.
buzz: The dune camping is the experience and the wind is relentless; check the closures for snowy plover nesting and air down your tires.

name: Buck Owens Crystal Palace
unique: Buck Owens' club and museum in Bakersfield, with his red silver sparkle guitar, a restaurant and live country music in the room that kept the Bakersfield sound alive.
buzz: The museum cases are free to browse and the shows are the draw; the food is better than a club restaurant needs to be.

name: Kern River Rafting
customer: Groups, families with teens, adventure seekers
unique: Class III and IV rapids on the river that flows out of the Sierra south of Sequoia, with a gorge section and a calmer lower run for first timers.
buzz: Outfitters say May and June are the biggest water and the lower river is the family trip; the water is cold and the canyon is hot.

name: Tule Elk State Reserve
unique: A preserve where a herd of tule elk survives on the valley floor, with a viewing platform and a fence line you can drive along.
buzz: The elk are visible most mornings and the reserve is a short detour from Interstate 5; bring binoculars and go early.

name: Forestiere Underground Gardens
unique: Ten acres of underground rooms, courtyards and fruit trees dug by one Sicilian immigrant with hand tools over 40 years to escape the valley heat.
buzz: Visitors are astonished it exists; the tour is the only way in and the temperature stays in the 70s while Fresno bakes outside.

name: Fresno County Blossom Trail
unique: A self guided drive through orchards in bloom, with farm stands selling oranges and almonds and a map that changes with what is flowering.
buzz: The bloom window is short and weather dependent; locals check the county blossom report before driving and go on a weekday.

name: Meux Home Museum
customer: House tour people, local history fans
unique: A Victorian house built by a Confederate surgeon who moved to Fresno, with original furniture, a carriage house and a garden in the middle of downtown.
buzz: The volunteers know the family and the house is a step back into 1890s Fresno; it is small and only open afternoons.

name: Emerald Bay
unique: A glacier carved bay on Lake Tahoe with the only island in the lake, a 1929 stone castle on the shore and turquoise water clear to 60 feet.
buzz: The overlook on the highway is the postcard and the Vikingsholm trail down is steep; the castle tour is worth timing and the parking is limited.

name: Apple Hill
unique: A loop of apple farms in the Sierra foothills where you pick your own, buy cider doughnuts and watch trees turn, 45 minutes from Sacramento.
buzz: October weekends are a traffic jam and the pie sells out; go on a weekday and start at the top of the loop.

name: Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
unique: The sawmill site where gold was found in 1848, with a replica mill, a mine tunnel, a blacksmith and a chance to pan for gold in the American River.
buzz: Panning is the reason children agree to the history; the park is shaded and the museum explains how the discovery changed the state.

name: Columbia State Historic Park
customer: History families, school groups, gold rush fans
unique: A gold rush town preserved as a living park, with a working stagecoach, a candy store in a brick 1850s building and shopkeepers in period dress.
buzz: The stagecoach ride and the panning are the family draws; the town is small and the summer heat is serious.

name: Railtown 1897
unique: A working roundhouse and steam shop where the locomotives that appeared in dozens of westerns are still maintained, with weekend steam excursions.
buzz: The roundhouse is the best part and the train ride runs on weekends; film fans come for the movie train history.

name: Don Pedro Lake
unique: A foothill reservoir with 160 miles of shoreline, a swim beach and a campground, warm enough for water sports by June.
buzz: The lake is the summer cooling off spot for the gold country; the water level drops late in the season and the wind comes up in the afternoon.
